subject: polity
title: Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35)
description: Six groups of Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural & Educational Rights, Right to Constitutional Remedies

content.overview: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12-35). They are justiciable and protect citizens against state arbitrariness.
keyPoints: Article 12: Definition of 'State' for Part III
Article 13: Laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void
Right to Equality (Articles 14-18): Equality before law, no discrimination, equal opportunity, abolition of untouchability, abolition of titles
Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22): Six freedoms, protection in conviction, life & personal liberty, education, safeguards in arrest
Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24): No human trafficking, no forced labour, no child labour below 14
Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28): Freedom of conscience, manage religious affairs, no tax for religion, no religious instruction in state-funded institutions
Cultural & Educational Rights (Articles 29-30): Protection of language/script/culture, minority educational rights
Right to Constitutional Remedies (Articles 32-35): Five writs, martial law restrictions, Parliament's power to modify

mnemonics.trick: E-F-E-R-C-R = Equality, Freedom, Exploitation, Religion, Cultural, Remedies
mnemonics.explanation: Remember: Equality (14-18), Freedom (19-22), Exploitation (23-24), Religion (25-28), Cultural (29-30), Remedies (32-35)

mnemonics.trick: SAMARA = Speech, Assembly, Movement, Residence, Association, Profession
mnemonics.explanation: Article 19 grants six freedoms: Speech & expression, Assembly, Movement, Residence, Association, Profession

mnemonics.trick: HMCQP = Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Quo Warranto, Prohibition
mnemonics.explanation: Five writs: Habeas Corpus (produce person), Mandamus (command public duty), Certiorari (quash order), Quo Warranto (question authority), Prohibition (stop lower court)
Some rights are only for citizens (15, 16, 19, 29, 30), others for all persons including non-citizens (14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25-28, 32)

quiz.question: Which article defines the term 'State' for Part III?
quiz.explanation: Article 12 defines 'State' for the purpose of Fundamental Rights

quiz.question: Article 19 is available to:
quiz.explanation: Article 19 (six freedoms) is available only to citizens, not non-citizens

quiz.question: Which writ means 'produce the person before the court'?
quiz.explanation: Habeas Corpus means 'you shall have the body' - produce the person before the court

quiz.question: Article 32 is called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by:
quiz.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution

quiz.question: Which article prohibits child labour below 14 years?
quiz.explanation: Article 24 prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, and hazardous occupations

timeline.event: Fundamental Rights came into force with Constitution
86th Amendment made Article 21A a Fundamental Right
